arXiv:2611.00299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topological spin textures that can be observed directly by magnetic microscopy and driven by fields and currents, which makes them a model system for fundamental physics and candidates for spintronic devices. 👤 Daniel Mills, Ifan Williams, Jacob Swain, Gabriel Matos, Enrico Rinaldi and Alexander Koziell-Pipe
Many quantum software development kits provide a suite of circuit optimisation passes. These passes have been highly optimised and tested in isolation. However, the order in which they are applied is left to the user, or else defined in general-purpose default pass sequences. While general-purpose sequences miss opportunities for optimisation which are particular to individual circuits, designing pass sequences bespoke to particular circuits requires exceptional knowledge about quantum circuit design and optimisation. Here we propose and demonstrate training a reinforcement learning agent to compose optimisation-pass sequences. 👤 Dinesh Sai Palli, Vardhan Nagulla, Sai Saketha Chandra Athkuri
Determining an unknown flow parameter from a limited number of experimental measurement data is an essential requirement for many engineering problems. Inverse physics-informed neural network (I-PINN) provide a mesh-free way unlike the usual adjoint- or conjugategradient-based methods by adding the unknown parameter as a trainable one along with other weights of the neural network during the training phase. In this paper, we study the effective sensor placement for a flow past a circular cylinder to recover the Reynolds number (𝑅𝑒) of the flow. We consider five zones in the flow independently and try to recover the 𝑅𝑒 from synthetic data obtained from the validated forward PINN. item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Ruidong Li, Shuai Yang, Wenyu Song, Zeyu Yan, Yuhao Wang, Zehao Yu, Li Chen, Zixun Xia, Zonglin Li, Shan Zhang, Jiaye Xu, Lining Yang, Weizhao Wang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Dong E. Liu, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, Hao Zhang
arXiv:2611.02411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

arXiv:2611.02804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, it was observed that, in non-collinear IrMn3, both the non-magnetic spin Hall effect (NMSHE) and the magnetic spin Hall effect (MSHE) exhibit oscillations as the triangularly ordered magnetic moments of IrMn3 evolve with temperature. These oscillations are strongly influenced by the magnetic properties at the interface between IrMn3 and the adjacent material. Permalloy (Py), a ferromagnet, and platinum (Pt), a paramagnet, were employed as adjacent layers. Such experimental analyses demonstrate the pioneering nature of this phenomenon, which is validated through magnetoresistance measurements performed under different experimental conditions.
